# FDG8091

> DO use `System.Uri` to represent URI and URL data.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.11 Uri.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1054, CA1055, CA1056
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Test profile: none, because test methods are public and take URLs as strings from test-case attributes, which cannot be Uri values; CA1054 reports such a parameter. CA1054 (parameters), CA1055 (return values) and CA1056 (properties) report a string in an externally visible member whose name contains a word such as uri, url or urn (probe with SDK 10.0.402). Strings whose names do not say they are URIs are not seen, so coverage is partial. Changing the type to Uri changes the public signature, so the fix is breaking.

## From the book

This applies to parameter types, property types, and return value types.

```csharp
public class Navigator {
  public Navigator(Uri initialLocation);
  public Uri CurrentLocation { get; }
  public Uri NavigateTo(Uri location);
}
```

> **Mark Alcazar:** `System.Uri` is a much safer and richer way of representing URIs. Extensive manipulation of URI-related data using plain strings has been shown to cause many security and correctness problems.
